title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Iran says at least four tankers hit mines and caught fire in Hormuz, and another vessel was reported burning off Khasab this morning, so the Gulf sea lane got riskier overnight. UAE November fuel prices land tomorrow with diesel already up 88% this year, while the first UAE flights back to Saudi have partly slipped after new Houthi strikes on Riyadh.

gauges.label: Brent crude, per barrel
gauges.note: Settled 29 Oct, down $0.44 (Reuters via Arabian Business)

gauges.label: UAE diesel per litre, October
gauges.note: Up 88.2% since January; November prices due 31 Oct (Arabian Business)

gauges.label: SCFI Persian Gulf & Red Sea index
gauges.note: 8 Oct, up 318% on a year earlier (Ti Insight)

gauges.label: Europe to Middle East airfreight rate
gauges.note: 11 Oct, up 85% year on year (Freightos via Ti Insight)

gauges.label: Khalifa Port throughput, 2025
gauges.note: Up 21.6%; now 34th in Lloyd's List Top 100 (AD Ports)

gauges.label: UPS international revenue per piece, Q3

stories.headline: Four tankers on fire after hitting mines in Hormuz; another ship burning off Khasab
body: Iran's armed forces said at least four tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours. Flags and exact timing were not clear. UKMTO also reported a dhow fire about 9 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman; it sank and the crew was evacuated.

This morning UKMTO reported an outbound vessel on fire about 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, cause unknown. Reports also say the US and Israel are preparing a possible week-long bombing campaign against Iran after the 3 November US midterms.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: mines, not just blockade checks, are now hitting ships. Expect war-risk and Gulf sea surcharges to stay high; keep urgent UAE imports on east-coast and Oman gateways.

stories.headline: Gulf container rates more than four times last year
body: The Shanghai index for the Persian Gulf and Red Sea service stood at 4,035 on 8 October, up 318% on a year earlier. It peaked at 4,180 on 24 September. The IMF now assumes Hormuz stays shut until March 2027.
Oman will not renew APM Terminals' Salalah concession, which expires on 1 November 2028.
stories.soWhat: Sea rates into the Gulf will not normalise soon. Keep sea quotes short-dated and indexed into 2027.

stories.headline: Khalifa Port climbs to 34th in world container ranking
body: Khalifa Port handled 6.6 million TEU in 2025, up 21.6%, the biggest rise among the world's top 40 ports. It rose five places to 34th in Lloyd's List Top 100. A CMA Terminals expansion will lift total port capacity to 10.5 million TEU.
stories.soWhat: Abu Dhabi is gaining as a container gateway. Make sure our Khalifa trucking and clearance offer is as sharp as our Jebel Ali one.

stories.headline: Saudi restart slips for flydubai as Houthis hit Riyadh again
body: flydubai has pushed its Riyadh and Dammam restart from 30 October to 1 November. Emirates still lists Jeddah from 30 October and Riyadh and Dammam from 8 November. Etihad stays off Saudi until 5 November.

On 29 October the Houthis claimed six attacks, including on Riyadh and Dammam airports. The coalition confirmed two ballistic missiles intercepted over Riyadh. From 8 to 25 October, 85.96% of Riyadh departures were cancelled.
stories.soWhat: New: the restart is already slipping. Keep UAE–KSA road as default and switch on air into Riyadh and Dammam only when flights actually run.

stories.headline: Gulf air capacity still 20% down, rates well up
body: WorldACD put Gulf air capacity in the week to 11 October 20% below late-February levels. Middle East and South Asia rates were 52% above a year earlier. Europe to Middle East rates were $3.12 a kg, up 85% on last year.
Riyadh freighter and widebody capacity fell 99%, from 3,925 to 26 tonnes, after the airport attacks (Rotate data via The Loadstar).
stories.soWhat: Air capacity is tight and paid for. Hold airfreight margins; do not chase volume with rate cuts.

stories.headline: UAE November fuel prices due tomorrow; diesel up 88% this year
body: The Fuel Price Committee announces November rates on Saturday 31 October. Diesel is Dh4.80 a litre in October, up from Dh2.55 in January. Super 98 is Dh4.40, against a record of Dh4.63 in July 2022.
Brent eased to $114.88 on 29 October, but December contracts have averaged about $107 in October against $102 in September.
stories.soWhat: Domestic and road costs are near records. Have the November fuel surcharge ready to move the day prices come out.

competitors.name: UPS
competitors.headline: Q3 international revenue per piece up 15%; guidance raised
body: UPS international revenue rose 7.1% to $5.0 billion, with a 14.9% margin and revenue per piece up 15%. Group revenue was $22.9 billion and UPS raised full-year guidance. Supply Chain Solutions revenue rose 18.2%, but profit fell after a $182 million goodwill charge.
competitors.soWhat: Integrators are making money on yield and surcharges, not volume. Our international express pricing has room to hold.

competitors.name: Maersk / Gemini
competitors.headline: Relaunches Asia–Middle East FM1 loop via Khor Fakkan; adds Jeddah to ME2
body: Gemini Cooperation restarted its FM1 service, suspended since early 2026, with eight ships of about 13,500 TEU calling Khor Fakkan. First sailing was 17 October. Maersk's ME2 adds Jeddah from 20 December, a new North Europe to Saudi link.
competitors.soWhat: Big carriers are routing UAE cargo through the east coast. Package Khor Fakkan arrivals with our trucking and clearance before rivals do.

competitors.name: Emirates Courier Express
competitors.headline: Pushes door-to-door service to Dubai e-commerce brands
body: Emirates SkyCargo's courier arm is signing Dubai online brands such as Squatwolf and Mayple Global, a Shopify-linked fulfilment platform, and counts Magrabi Optical as a customer. No volumes were given.
competitors.soWhat: An airline-backed express rival is chasing our cross-border e-commerce SMEs. Defend these accounts with Shopify integration and GCC transit-time guarantees.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Latest result: record Q2 revenue of Dh1.83 billion
body: Revenue rose 22% to Dh1.83 billion in Q2 2026 and net profit was Dh47 million. Q3 results are not yet out.
competitors.soWhat: Compare our Q3 international yield with UPS's +15% per piece when results land.

opportunities.title: East-coast and Oman gateways
opportunities.text: Mines in Hormuz and Gemini's Khor Fakkan call push cargo east. Sell port-plus-trucking from Khor Fakkan and Sohar into Dubai.

opportunities.title: Khalifa Port growth
opportunities.text: Khalifa grew 21.6% to 6.6 million TEU. Win Abu Dhabi importers with clearance and last-mile bundles.

opportunities.title: KSA road while air is down
opportunities.text: Riyadh air capacity fell 99%. UAE–KSA road is the reliable option; sell it on fixed terms.

opportunities.title: Pricing power in air and express
opportunities.text: Air rates are 52–85% above last year and UPS lifted yield 15%. Room to hold margins.

opportunities.title: E-commerce SME defence
opportunities.text: Emirates Courier Express is targeting Dubai online brands. Offer integrated shipping plus GCC delivery to keep them.

watchouts.title: Mines in Hormuz
watchouts.text: At least four tankers hit mines and another ship burned off Khasab today. Sea transits and insurance get worse.

watchouts.title: Post-midterm escalation
watchouts.text: Reports point to a possible US–Israel campaign on Iran after 3 November. Treat next week as a risk window.

watchouts.title: Fuel prices tomorrow
watchouts.text: November UAE fuel prices come out on 31 October; diesel is already Dh4.80.

watchouts.title: KSA air restart slipping
watchouts.text: flydubai moved Riyadh and Dammam to 1 November after new strikes. Do not promise air into KSA yet.

watchouts.title: Airline-backed express rival
watchouts.text: Emirates Courier Express is winning Dubai e-commerce brands with door-to-door service.

moves.title: Move the fuel surcharge on 31 October
moves.text: Publish the November road and domestic fuel surcharge the day UAE prices are out.

moves.title: Keep Gulf sea quotes short and indexed
moves.text: Mines are now hitting ships and the Gulf index is up 318%. Do not fix sea rates past November.

moves.title: Launch a Khor Fakkan arrival package
moves.text: Gemini's FM1 now calls Khor Fakkan. Offer clearance plus trucking to Dubai and Abu Dhabi to top importers.

moves.title: Hold KSA air until flights run
moves.text: Keep Riyadh and Dammam express on road; switch on air only once Emirates and flydubai actually operate.

moves.title: Hold air and express margins
moves.text: Market rates are 52–85% up and UPS lifted yield 15%. Avoid discounting on contract renewals.

moves.title: Protect Dubai e-commerce SMEs
moves.text: Call top cross-border online brands this week with an integration and GCC transit offer.

note: Read from today's news. Check against our own numbers before acting.
